record.context_brief: When a Steiner tree can be an MDM
record.original_question: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be a compact totally disconnected set for which there exist at least two different Steiner trees connecting A (call them S and T). A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Can one of the Steiner trees (for example S) also arise as a solution to a maximal distance minimization problem (for some choice of r > 0 and some compact target set M)?

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set M ⊂ Rd and a given positive number r > 0, consider the problem of finding a connected compact
set Σ of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such that

                                M ⊂ Br (Σ),

where Br (Σ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of the set Σ. We refer to such a set Σ as a Maximal distance minimizer
(MDM or r-minimizer).

Question 2.8. Let A ⊂ Rd be a compact totally disconnected set with at least two Steiner trees, say S and T . Can S be a
solution to the maximal distance minimizers problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a compact set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and a fixed real number $r>0$, a maximal distance minimizer (or $r$-minimizer) for $M$ is a connected compact set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected compact sets satisfying $M\subset B_r(\Sigma)$, where $B_r(\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\Sigma)\le r\}$ denotes the closed $r$-neighborhood of $\Sigma$. A Steiner tree for a compact set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is a connected compact set of minimal $\mathcal{H}^1$-length that contains $A$.

Suppose $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is a compact totally disconnected set admitting at least two distinct Steiner trees $S$ and $T$. Determine whether it is possible for $S$ to coincide with a maximal distance minimizer for some compact set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and some $r>0$; that is, does there exist a choice of $M$ and $r>0$ such that $S$ is an $r$-minimizer for $M$?
artifact.category_tag: Maximal distance minimizers and Steiner trees
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a November 2025 collection of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers by Y. Teplitskaya, where it is explicitly stated as an open question. No subsequent literature resolving it was found.
